head: The sentence with no adjectives
text: ‘I dine where my Collectors dine.’ Seven words, and the Silchar Club door swung on them, and a settlement officer’s sons will walk through it all their lives. Of everything the year built in stone and paper, the thing most likely to outlast the Empire is a sentence.

head: Two lines, correctly spent
text: The honours circular allowed two names and you spent them where the work was. Somewhere up the hill a committee blinked, and passed it, and the List that year said something true. Nobody will ever know it was difficult. That is the job, done.

head: The wire he can publish
text: The Commissioner concurs and will answer for it. Ormsby kept the form of that telegram, they say, in his despatch-box through three districts. A young Collector backed once in the dark at midnight is an officer made for twenty years — and he will govern, someday, as he was governed.

head: The paragraph that ended a career
text: Forty villages came out of the water dry, and the order that dried them was one paragraph long, and it retired a man of twenty-six years’ service as surely as any court-martial. The Service has forgiven you the result. The manner it has merely recorded.

head: The file number you keep by heart
text: The famine that did not happen has no monument; prevention never does. There is only a file with His Honour’s initials and one line — this is what the reserve is for — and, in Marwan, several thousand people who will never know they were the subject of the year’s best decision.

head: The three weeks
text: The Code was satisfied, and the Code was late, and the difference is counted in a column no return prints. Petherick’s one word — wait — carries your concurrence beneath it forever. You have learned what the Code is for: it is for sharing out the blame that foresight would have made unnecessary.

head: The scale-beam
text: One commutation, argued in full, against the whole weight of the law’s convenience. The Kurmi breaks stone in the Andamans and is alive, and a dozen ledgers in the Division grew more careful the month the order came down. Dass’s forwarding sentence is in your desk. You have never needed to reread it.

head: Two days and a horse
text: A confidential report wintered in a drawer, and a boy at Kotra found his feet never knowing why the Commissioner came. The Service’s oldest ledger carries one more entry payable forward — the same entry, in fact, that was once made out to you, now countersigned.

head: The tin box
text: He kept a boundary decision in a young sahib’s uncertain hand for fourteen years, against the day the hand came back. The marigolds, the tea, the grandson presented at the salute: whatever the Gazette decides this year, that hour in the old man’s courtyard was the inspection that mattered, and the marks were kind.

head: The other Commissioner
text: The Division was governed twice over this year — once from the office, once from the drawing-room, and the second administration ran the smoother. Her card on a hall table did what your warrant could not. The Service pays her nothing and could not function a fortnight without her kind, and both of you know which of its two officers Sonepore will remember.

head: The cut string
text: Twenty years of paper — Kotra, the district, the Division, patient as ivy — ended in one draft and a bow. The Lala keeps the cancelled account, they say, in the steel almirah still: not as a debt now, but as a curiosity. A client who got away is the rarest item in his collection.

head: The graveyard series
text: The oilcloth bundle lies in Government House under His Honour’s own key, in the series where careers are buried alive. You put it there yourself, which is the only reason you are still at your desk. Contrive not to be a fool twice. You have the sentence by heart. It is the cheapest knighthood-price never paid.

head: The second fair copy
text: A clerkship, a well, four minutes of fire — and somewhere, existing or not, a second copy the exact size and shape of the rest of your career. The old man salaamed and went. You have caught yourself, twice this cold weather, reading the New Dawn first for a paragraph that is never in it. Yet.

head: What the river charged
text: The steamer’s stove paddle-box was rebuilt in a month; the cough the storm passage left has kept its own calendar since. The Surgeon’s report used the word ‘reckless’ inside a citation, which is the Service’s way of saying it would prefer its heroes insurable. Silchar remembers the arrival. Your chest remembers the fare.

head: Good for it
text: The greys went, the table plainened, the instalments marched — and in the Bank’s Calcutta ledgers, against your name, stands the annotation that outvalues a paragraph in the Gazette: good for it. The Agent has never once said the words aloud. He merely renews, now, without reading the file, which is a banker’s love letter.

head: The figure in the almirah
text: The knighthood came — and in the steel almirah at Chhota Nagra your paper ages on, patient, compounding, asking for nothing. Sir is a fine word. The Lala’s ledger has a column for it now, and the column, like all his columns, is merely waiting.

head: The tab you will never see
text: The High Court’s language went into the Secretariat’s file on you under a tab of its own: the Commissioner who upheld an order he knew was bad, for the sake of a policy. The policy was real. So is the tab. Files at altitude forget nothing; they merely wait to be relevant.

head: The photograph of the empty street
text: Two pages in the London illustrated papers: bunting, bayonets, and no one at all. Nobody blamed you in writing; the tour’s history gave your three hours one sentence in the passive voice. You have read the sentence. You are its subject.

head: The interview that is in no file
text: Two hours, no clerks, three practical things settled, and the town’s hartals peaceable year after year for reasons no despatch records. The pleader-president keeps your measure as you keep his. Somewhere far above you both, men who have never met describe each other in proclamations.

head: Eight points off the harvest rate
text: A third of the societies failed, as the Registrar’s own arithmetic promised. The rest did the quiet revolutionary thing: the bazaar’s rate dropped eight points to compete, across every village in the Division, including the ones with no society at all. Reform, when it finally works, sends no wire.

head: The two names
text: Merit alone, no varnish, and half the cadre furious on two different arithmetics. Ten years on, one of the two is a district officer the province quotes, and the lists you wrote read like prophecy, as honest lists do. Nobody remembers the storm. Both men do.

head: The evidence in your voice
text: Two hours before their lordships, and the best passage in the Division’s memorandum was another man’s argument delivered over your signature, acknowledged nowhere, understood everywhere. The boycott had nothing to burn and Government nothing to enter. Some services between officers have no file. This one has a blue-book, unattributed.

head: The effigy at Silchar
text: He went because you said go, and the evidence was the best the Commission heard, and the effigy burned on schedule. The blue-book keeps the three hours; Silchar keeps the evening. You have both learned the weight of your advice, which is a thing better learned cheaper.

head: The sirkar's house
text: No budget head, one irregular audit answer, and two hundred children of the fever year raised creed-blind under a pensioned havildar-major. Asked years later where they were from, they say: the sirkar’s house. The exchequer has bought many loyalties dearer and none at par.
